key_insight: A deep truncated FBSDE solver stabilizes high-dimensional nonlinear PDE solving by decoupling strong forward-backward coupling with gradient truncation, fictitious-play averaging, and pathwise consistency shortcuts.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more robust numerical tool for convection-dominated and strongly coupled PDE/FBSDE systems where standard deep solvers can become unstable or suffer from vanishing gradients.
method: Gradient-truncated iterative decoupling to reduce unstable feedback from parameter-dependent forward paths.
Fictitious-play averaging to preserve coupled dynamics while improving optimization stability.
Pathwise consistency loss to add local gradient shortcuts and mitigate vanishing gradients.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy and stability in low- and high-dimensional experiments, including robust performance on strongly coupled problems, along with a residual-based error estimate and conditional convergence results.
watch_item: The convergence guarantee is conditional and the pathwise consistency term is not required for the theoretical fully discrete convergence, so implementation choices and training stability may depend on problem structure.
paper_title: Deep Truncated FBSDE Method: A Robust Solver for High-Dimensional Nonlinear PDEs and Fully Coupled FBSDEs
